en: Air is a mixture of gases that has measurable mass and takes up physical space, which is why an inflated balloon weighs more than a deflated one.
Melting solid ice into liquid water is a physical change because the H2O molecules remain exactly the same and no new chemical substance is formed.
Evaporation is a physical change that happens at the surface of a liquid at almost any temperature, not just when the liquid reaches its boiling point.
Dissolving solid sugar in water creates a liquid mixture where the sugar molecules remain intact and can be completely recovered by evaporating the liquid water.
Not all metals are magnetic, as common metallic elements like copper, aluminum, and gold are not attracted to a magnet despite being solid metals.
Although invisible gases expand to fill their container, the gas particles still have measurable mass and take up physical space just like solids and liquids.
Boiling liquid water produces bubbles of water vapor gas, which is a physical change of state rather than a chemical change creating a new substance.
Rusting iron is a chemical change because the solid metal reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide, a completely new brown substance.
Solutions are not always liquids, because brass is a solid solution created by mixing melted copper and zinc metals together to form a single solid.
A clear, colorless liquid is not always pure water, because clear liquids like white vinegar or rubbing alcohol are actually mixtures of different substances.
Breaking a solid piece of chalk into smaller dust particles changes only its physical size and shape, not its chemical composition or fundamental properties.
Burning wood does not make matter disappear, because the solid wood chemically changes into new substances like ash, water vapor, and carbon dioxide gas.
